title: Data-Center Market Is Booming Amid Shift to Cloud
summary: The data-center market is experiencing a boom driven by the shift to cloud computing, even as many businesses are moving IT operations online. This has led to increased demand and consolidation among data-center operators as co-location service providers acquire facilities to lease space to major cloud services like Amazon.com Inc. and Microsoft Corp. The sector is seeing more deals as data-center landlords and cloud providers seek more facilities.

title: Synchrony Says Walmart to Drop Lawsuit Against Credit-Card Issuer
summary: Synchrony Financial announced that Walmart Inc. has agreed to dismiss a lawsuit against the bank, which had alleged that Synchrony breached terms of their credit-card deal. Walmart was seeking at least $800 million in damages. This development comes after Walmart decided last year to replace Synchrony as its exclusive credit-card issuer with Capital One Financial Corp.

title: Netflix Just Made a Truly Radical Change Affecting Millions of New Subscribers, and It's Totally Brilliant. (Or Maybe Insane--Time Will Tell)
summary: Netflix has implemented a significant change by no longer allowing new subscribers to pay via iTunes, aiming to avoid the substantial "Apple tax" of 15% to 30% on subscription revenue. This strategic move, which could save Netflix hundreds of millions, shifts new users to subscribe directly through the Netflix app, cutting Apple out of its commission. While potentially risking some new subscribers, Netflix is betting that its strong demand across platforms will outweigh any losses and make the decision financially brilliant in the long run.

title: Is Apple Still a ‘forever’ Company? How About Facebook?
summary: This article questions the "forever company" thesis for tech giants like Apple and Facebook, highlighting recent market shifts and challenges. It discusses how Apple's plunging shares due to demand issues in China and Nokia's past trajectory suggest even dominant companies face significant hurdles. The piece also explores the concept of S-curves in technology, suggesting that while current tech giants are strong, a new S-curve, potentially augmented reality or AI, could reset the competitive landscape.

title: ADT Unveils New Command and Control Security System, Replacing ADT Pulse
summary: ADT announced the launch of its new ADT Command Panel & Control Platform (ADT Command) at CES 2019, replacing the previous ADT Pulse system. This new smart home security system integrates with a suite of smart security and home automation products, including ADT Go, ADT Video Doorbell, and voice control with Amazon Alexa and Google Home, offering advanced features like geofencing technology and an interactive crime map. The system focuses on enhanced protection, control, and connectivity for customers.

title: Microsoft and Kroger want to show you Minority Report-style ads
summary: Microsoft and Kroger are partnering to develop high-tech grocery stores that will feature digital shelving displays with real-time pricing and personalized advertisements, reminiscent of "Minority Report." These ads will be tailored to individual customers based on demographics and, for opted-in users, previous purchase history, utilizing facial recognition and AI. While not cashierless like Amazon Go, the stores aim to enhance the shopping experience with guided navigation and in-app scanning for faster checkout.

title: For Many Builders, Smart Homes Now Come Standard
summary: New-home builders are increasingly integrating smart home technology as a standard feature due to its widespread adoption and affordability. Companies like Meritage Homes and Lennar are partnering with tech giants such as Amazon, Google, and Apple to offer various smart devices and services, aiming to meet consumer demand and differentiate new constructions from existing homes. This shift is driven by consumer expectations and the decreasing cost of smart home tech, making it a compelling baseline amenity for new builds.

title: Resideo Unveils A New Degree Of Whole Home Comfort At CES 2019
summary: Resideo announced its new Honeywell Home T-Series Smart Thermostats (T9 and T10 Pro) at CES 2019, featuring innovative wireless smart room sensors. These thermostats aim to provide whole-home comfort by adjusting temperatures where and when needed, optimizing for sleep at night and energy savings when away. The T9 model offers DIY installation, while the T10 Pro is professionally installed and includes humidity and ventilation controls.

title: Vuzix announces the launch of consumer version of its Blade augmented reality smart glasses
summary: Vuzix has launched the consumer version of its Blade augmented reality smart glasses for USD$999.99, featuring proprietary waveguide optics, a full-color display, and an HD camera. The glasses integrate with an Android-based OS, a companion app for customization and notifications, and are expected to ship in early February 2019. Vuzix is also partnering with Amazon for Alexa integration and AccuWeather for AR weather experiences, highlighting the Blade's potential for both prosumers and consumers as a step towards wearable computing.

title: Best Consumer Discretionary ETFs for Q1 2021
summary: This article identifies the best consumer discretionary ETFs for Q1 2021 based on performance over the past year. The top three ETFs highlighted are IBUY, ONLN, and NERD, which primarily focus on online retail and digital entertainment, showcasing their strong returns and key holdings. These ETFs provide diversified exposure to non-essential goods and services, a sector that has outperformed the broader market.

title: Amazon CEO Jeff Bezos, Wife MacKenzie Set to Divorce
summary: Amazon.com Inc. CEO Jeff Bezos and his wife MacKenzie Bezos announced their decision to divorce after a long trial separation. The announcement comes as Amazon recently became Wall Street's most valuable company, and Jeff Bezos' fortune has soared to over $160 billion. The article also touches on Amazon's growth and diversification since its founding in 1994.

title: JP Morgan's Dimon hosted a private dinner for pharma executives, and a major topic was Amazon
summary: Jamie Dimon hosted a private dinner for pharmaceutical executives, including those from Eli Lilly, Pfizer, and Johnson & Johnson, ahead of J.P. Morgan's health-care conference. A major topic of discussion was Amazon's ambitions in the health-care market and the J.P. Morgan-Amazon-Berkshire Hathaway health partnership. Dimon expressed the group's desire to lower health-care costs, a sentiment echoed by attending executives like Eli Lilly CEO Dave Ricks, who encouraged corporate America to take a more active role in employee health benefits.

title: Exclusive: West Elm Hotel checks into Bay Area with Oakland groundbreaking
summary: The West Elm Hotel has broken ground in Uptown Oakland, marking the brand's entry into the Bay Area. This four-star hotel will be located near Square's new offices in Uptown Station and thousands of residential units under construction. The article highlights the trend of retailers expanding into the hotel industry.

title: The Bath & Body Works Semi-Annual Sale Is Ending Soon, So Snag Those $10 Candles While You Still Can
summary: The Bath & Body Works Semi-Annual Sale is coming to an end on January 18th, offering significant discounts of up to 75% off. Shoppers can find deals like $4 body care, $4 Wallflower refills, and 3-Wick Candles for $10, which were originally $25. The sale also brings back discontinued fragrances and provides an opportunity to stock up on new scents for the year.

title: JB Hunt acquires ‘big and bulky’ last-mile provider
summary: J.B. Hunt has acquired Cory 1st Choice Home Delivery for $100 million to expand its final mile delivery capabilities for "big and bulky" products, especially furniture. This strategic investment aims to address the growing demand in e-commerce for oversized items and mitigate issues like damaged deliveries. The acquisition includes 14 warehouses and leverages over 1,000 independent contractors to perform more than 2 million annual deliveries.

title: With Google project, Minnesota joins the boom in megasized data centers
summary: Minnesota is set to join the growing trend of megasized data centers with Google Inc.'s proposed project near the Sherco power generating station in Becker, Minn. This $600 million facility will consume significant electricity and contribute to the regional boom in "hyperscale" data centers being built by major tech companies. While these centers employ few people once operational, their construction phases provide hundreds of jobs, particularly for skilled electricians, and are critical for the infrastructure of cloud-based computing.

title: Walmart and CVS Split Over Pricing
summary: Walmart and CVS Health's partnership has ended due to a dispute over prescription drug pricing, leading CVS pharmacies to no longer include Walmart pharmacies in their network for most consumers. CVS stock fell 1.5 percent following the announcement, with CVS citing Walmart's requested rates as leading to higher costs for their clients and consumers. Despite the split, CVS stated its retail pharmacy network remains robust, with over 63,000 other pharmacies providing ample access for its members.

title: BlackRock’s Fink looks to a ‘deep bench’ to pick heir
summary: Larry Fink, BlackRock's CEO, is looking to his firm's "deep bench" of executives to name a successor, with Mark Wiedman's recent promotion positioning him at the top of the list. Despite this, other senior figures including Mark McCombe, Mark Wiseman, Rob Goldstein, Rob Kapito, and Rich Kushel remain in contention. The article details the backgrounds, key accomplishments, and potential challenges for each of these possible heirs to the leadership of the $6.4tn asset management group.

title: Sears staves off demise, but Volusia Mall store still closing
summary: Sears has secured a reprieve from bankruptcy thanks to a bid from its chairman, Eddie Lampert, which could save approximately 400 stores and tens of thousands of jobs. However, despite this broader development, the Sears department store at Volusia Mall is still slated to close in March as part of previously announced closures. This closure is one of 80 national locations Sears Holdings plans to shutter, while local Sears Hometown and Outlet stores, which are separate entities, will remain open.

title: Netflix beats on subscriber growth, but misses slightly on revenue — stock falls after hours
summary: Netflix reported mixed fourth-quarter 2018 earnings, beating EPS estimates and subscriber additions but falling short on revenue. The company’s stock dropped after hours due to the revenue miss and lower-than-expected guidance for Q1 2019. Despite increased content spending and cash burn, Netflix saw strong international subscriber growth and plans to improve free cash flow after 2019.

title: Semiconductor Company Wiliot Raises $30 Million, Demos Sticker-Sized Bluetooth Sensor Tag
summary: Wiliot, a fabless semiconductor company, has raised $30 million in Series B funding, bringing its total to $50 million, with investments from Amazon Web Services, Samsung Venture Investment Corp, and Avery Dennison. The company demonstrated its sticker-sized Bluetooth sensor tag, an ARM processor powered by ambient radio frequencies, at NRF 2019. This technology enables disposable, battery-free electronics for IoT, offering new ways for consumers and manufacturers to interact with products and track them in real-time.

title: Amazon pushing hard into ocean shipping, making it easier for Chinese goods to get to you
summary: Amazon has significantly expanded its ocean shipping services from China to the U.S., reportedly sending nearly 4.7 million cartons of consumer goods in the past year. This move is part of Amazon's broader strategy to control its entire transportation network, offering a soup-to-nuts service that eliminates middlemen for goods manufactured in China. Experts believe this development will transform the global e-commerce landscape and accelerate globalization by enabling small Chinese factories to sell directly to American consumers.

title: First battery-free Bluetooth sticker sensor tag demonstrated
summary: Wiliot, a semiconductor innovator, has demonstrated the first-ever sticker-sized, battery-free Bluetooth sensor tag powered by scavenging ambient radio frequencies. This technology allows for low-cost, disposable electronics capable of connecting products with packaging, enabling new IoT applications. AWS, Samsung, and Avery Dennison have invested in Wiliot, recognizing the potential of these tags for real-time tracking, interactive consumer engagement, and automated product management.

title: Corsair Vengeance 5180 gaming PC review: "A beautiful machine with performance to match"
summary: This article reviews the Corsair Vengeance 5180 gaming PC, highlighting its powerful components, excellent dual-chamber design, and brilliant RGB lighting. While acknowledging its large size and non-overclockable CPU, the review praises its performance at 1080p and 1440p and its overall value for gamers seeking a pre-built machine.

title: Starboard, Elliott Management Call on eBay to Shed StubHub, Classifieds
summary: Activist investors Starboard and Elliott Management are urging eBay to divest its StubHub ticketing and classified-ads businesses. This move comes as eBay's shares have underperformed, with the company struggling to redefine itself beyond its auction house origins and compete with e-commerce giants like Amazon. The proposed changes by these hedge funds could lead to a significant restructuring of the company.

title: 20 Things You Didn’t Know about Sierra Trading Post
summary: This article details 20 lesser-known facts about Sierra Trading Post, from its founding by Keith and Bobbi Richardson in 1986 to its acquisition by TJX Companies in 2012. It covers the company's growth, catalog innovations, relocation to Cheyenne, early online presence, community involvement, unique company culture, and the founders' passion for breeding German Shorthaired Pointers. The article highlights Sierra's commitment to quality outdoor products and its significant contributions to local economies.

title: Weis Markets rolls out aggressive price cuts
summary: Weis Markets has implemented its most aggressive price reduction program to date, cutting prices on over 7,000 products to compete with rivals like Giant, Wegmans, Aldi, and Walmart. This "Low, Low Price" program follows a previous $101 million investment in store upgrades and technology, and aims to attract price-sensitive shoppers and retain loyal customers amidst increasing competition and rising food prices. The company reported a significant profit increase of 200% in the same quarter of the prior year, suggesting a positive financial position for this strategic move.

title: Elliott pushes for organizational changes at eBay after taking $1.4B stake
summary: Activist hedge fund Elliott Management Corp. has acquired a $1.4 billion stake in eBay Inc. and is pushing for significant organizational changes, including the sale of its online classifieds unit and StubHub ticket marketplace. Elliott believes these units would be more valuable as independent companies and that the divestitures would allow eBay to focus more sharply on its core e-commerce marketplace. The firm also recommends operational improvements and believes these changes could nearly double eBay's stock price.

title: The Ultimate Digital Transformation: Microsoft Helps Kroger Become Tech Company
summary: Kroger, America's largest grocery retailer, is undergoing a significant digital transformation by partnering with Microsoft to become a technology company. They are developing and selling cloud-based "Retail as a Service" (RaaS) solutions, powered by Microsoft Azure and IoT, to other retailers. This initiative aims to redefine the shopping experience through innovations like paperless smart shelves and hyper-personalization, creating new revenue opportunities beyond traditional grocery operations.

title: Sonos Amp Streaming Amplifier Review
summary: The Sonos Amp streaming amplifier is reviewed, highlighting its versatility and ease of integration into Sonos multiroom audio systems, despite some limitations in EQ and sound with certain speakers. This new device replaces the Connect:Amp, offering enhanced features and design improvements based on extensive feedback from custom integrators and DIY enthusiasts, effectively bridging the gap between consumer preferences and professional installation needs.

title: Synchrony Says Walmart to Drop Lawsuit Against Credit-Card Issuer
summary: Synchrony Financial announced that Walmart Inc. has agreed to dismiss a lawsuit against the bank, which alleged that Synchrony breached the terms of their credit-card deal. Walmart had sought at least $800 million in damages. This development follows Walmart's decision last year to replace Synchrony as its exclusive credit-card issuer with Capital One Financial Corp.

title: JPMorgan spinoff Kadena puts blockchain on AWS—and on the table for small and medium-sized businesses
summary: Kadena, a JPMorgan spinoff, is making blockchain technology accessible to small and medium-sized businesses by moving its development platform to Amazon Web Services (AWS), aiming to reduce development costs. This move allows companies, including those in healthcare, to experiment with and implement rudimentary blockchain solutions with ease. The company hopes to democratize blockchain access, moving beyond the current landscape where adoption has been primarily by larger firms due to high development costs.

title: Amazon Stock Rises as the 'Scout' Delivery Robot Is Unveiled
summary: Amazon announced the launch of its new delivery robot, "Scout," a cooler-sized ground unit designed for autonomous package delivery, initially accompanied by an Amazon employee. This announcement led to a 0.91 percent rise in Amazon's stock prices. The article also mentions other strong performers in the Entrepreneur Index™, including NVIDIA Corp. and Analog Devices, while J.M. Smucker Company, OReilly Auto Parts, and Brown-Forman Corp saw declines.

title: REIT Warehouse Logistics Being Redefined by Prologis
summary: Prologis, a leading logistics REIT, is redefining warehouse logistics by developing multi-story distribution centers in urban areas to meet the rising demand for faster e-commerce delivery. Their "Georgetown Crossroads" project in Seattle, the first U.S. multi-story warehouse serviceable by tractor-trailer trucks, highlights a strategy to densify sites in land-constrained metropolitan areas. This approach addresses the need to be closer to consumers and overcomes the limitations of traditional single-story warehouses on city outskirts, though it involves higher land acquisition and construction costs.

title: Why You Should Include ETFs in Your Portfolio
summary: ETFs offer a convenient and easy way to diversify a portfolio, combining features of individual stocks and mutual funds. They allow investors to participate in entire sectors, avoid single stock risk, and benefit from lower fees and greater tax efficiency compared to traditional mutual funds. The article also covers how to choose and purchase ETFs, as well as several investing strategies.

title: Caterpillar, Nvidia Warnings Send Wall Street Tumbling
summary: U.S. stocks tumbled following warnings from Caterpillar and Nvidia, which highlighted concerns about a slowing Chinese economy and the impact of tariffs on corporate profits. Caterpillar missed profit estimates due to softening demand in China and rising costs, while Nvidia cut its revenue forecast due to weak demand and lower data center sales. This sent major indexes like the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq Composite lower, despite overall positive earnings reports.

title: What’s Changed: 2019 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Data Management Solutions for Analytics
summary: This article reviews the 2019 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Data Management Solutions for Analytics (DMSA), highlighting key changes since the previous report. It discusses shifts in vendor positions, new entrants, and removals, focusing on the evolution of major players like Oracle, Microsoft, Amazon Web Services, SAP, Teradata, IBM, Snowflake, Google, and MarkLogic. The article also touches upon the general trends in DMSA, emphasizing the growing importance of cloud and the diverse approaches taken by niche and leading providers.

title: FedEx Introduces Way for Retailers to Outrace Amazon in Delivery
summary: FedEx has introduced a new late-night shipping option for retailers, allowing them to offer next-day delivery for online orders placed as late as midnight. This initiative aims to help retailers compete with Amazon's fast delivery services, with FedEx emphasizing its growth strategy outside of its business with Amazon. The company sees potential in helping other businesses reduce delivery times and expects a significant increase in U.S. package volume by 2025.

title: Fidelity’s Steve Buller Built a Career on Actively Outperforming
summary: This article features an interview with Steve Buller, a long-serving portfolio manager at Fidelity Investments, discussing his two decades managing the Fidelity Real Estate Investment Portfolio Fund. Buller reflects on the fund's outperformance, the challenges of REIT acceptance, and how major market events have shaped his investment style. He also shares his insights on trending sectors, the impact of international sell-offs, and the future of fund management in a changing technological and financial landscape.

title: Activist Investors Urge eBay To Separate StubHub And Classifieds Businesses
summary: Activist investor Elliott Management Corporation is urging eBay to restructure by separating its StubHub and Classifieds businesses from its core Marketplace platform to unlock shareholder value. The proposal, supported by another hedge fund, Starboard Value LP, suggests this move, along with cost-cutting and increased share repurchases, could significantly boost eBay's stock performance. This push follows the successful PayPal spin-off in 2015, which was also championed by an activist investor.

title: Why Advanced Micro Devices might be important for service providers
summary: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) is becoming increasingly important for service providers due to its high-performance server processors like Epyc, which are crucial for hyperscale cloud players and data center updates. The company reported strong financial results in 2018, with significant growth in its data center business, and expects further adoption with its upcoming "Rome" processor, which offers improved performance and socket compatibility. As operators like AT&T, Sprint, and Comcast transform their networks with generic hardware, AMD's server technology is poised to play a key role in their data center evolution.
